title: What happens if you never get out of bed?

lines.text: Three weeks in bed. Thirty years older. What happens if you never get up?
Day one is bliss. No alarm, no stairs.
In 1966, five fit young men in Dallas stayed in bed for three weeks.
Their fitness crashed more than thirty years of ageing later did.
Stay longer and your bones lose about one percent a month.
But eight weeks of training fixed it. That's why heart patients now get up fast.
You're stronger than ever. Comment what stupid shenanigans Gary should try tomorrow.

experiment.note: New bedroom set and lie pose; jog pose for the turn. Hypothesis: a number-first hook ('3 weeks in bed. 30 years older.') beats a question.

facts.claim: Dallas Bed Rest and Training Study (1966): five healthy 20-year-old men, 3 weeks of strict bed rest; VO2max fell 27%, then rose 45% with 8 weeks of training
facts.source: McGuire et al. / Mitchell, Levine & McGuire, Circulation 2019 https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6814251/

facts.claim: At the 30-year follow-up their fitness had fallen only ~12% with ageing: 3 weeks of bed rest at 20 did more harm than 30 years of ageing
The study helped replace bed rest with cardiac rehabilitation for heart-attack patients
Bed rest bone mineral loss averages about 1-1.5% per month
